summary.name: HAProxy
summary.one_liner: HAProxy is a free, high-performance reverse proxy and load balancer for TCP and HTTP-based applications, widely used for high-traffic sites.
use_cases: Load balancing traffic across multiple backend web servers
Providing high availability for TCP and HTTP applications
Terminating SSL/TLS and managing certificates with ACME
Monitoring and troubleshooting live proxy traffic
Running a high-throughput edge proxy for very busy websites
summary.what_it_does: HAProxy is a reverse proxy offering high availability, load balancing, and proxying for TCP and HTTP applications. The page describes it as particularly suited to very high-traffic sites, with event-driven, multi-threaded architecture and claims of 2 million requests/s over SSL and 100 Gbps forwarded traffic in a single AWS Graviton2 test. It supports ACME certificate handling (DNS-01, dns-persist-01), QUIC/HTTP3, HTTP/2, and an OpenTelemetry filter. Release notes cover dynamic backends configurable via CLI (3.4), persistent stats across reloads and KTLS (3.3), and CPU-scaling improvements. The project offers LTS (even-numbered, 5-year support) and stable (odd-numbered, 12-18 month) branches.
notable: LTS branches maintained for 5 years, with odd-numbered stable branches maintained 12-18 months
Dynamic backends manageable from the CLI without reloads (3.4 LTS)
Commercial options: HAProxy Enterprise, HAProxy ALOHA hardware/virtual appliance, and paid support
Performance packages built against AWS-LC for Debian, Ubuntu, and RHEL
caveats: Commercial support, HAProxy Enterprise, and ALOHA appliances are paid offerings; the core project is free
Performance Packages are provided by HAProxy Technologies for latest Debian, Ubuntu, and soon RHEL, not mainstream distros
